name: Skill Retrieval Augmentation (SRA) / SR-Agents and SRA-Bench
venue: arXiv:2604.24594 (cs.CL; cs.AI). Preprint; v1 submitted 27 Apr 2026, v2 last revised 21 May 2026. No peer-reviewed venue identified as of retrieval.
authors_affiliation: Weihang Su, Jianming Long, Qingyao Ai (corresponding), Qiaozhi He, Yichen Tang, Changyue Wang, Yiteng Tu, Yingbo Wang, Yiqun Liu. Primary affiliation: Department of Computer Science and Technology, Tsinghua University; several authors (Weihang Su, Qiaozhi He, Yingbo Wang) also ByteDance Inc.
code_url: https://github.com/oneal2000/SR-Agents (MIT license; ships SRA-Bench under data/bench/; dataset mirror at https://huggingface.co/datasets/WeihangSu/SRA-Bench; project site https://sr-agents.github.io)
maintained_repo_url: https://github.com/oneal2000/SR-Agents (78 stars / 9 forks at retrieval time; last commit 2026-05-21; release v1.0.0 2026-05-13). Project site: https://sr-agents.github.io
task_domain: Agentic AI / tool-use, but evaluated as a capability-augmentation pipeline spanning theorem-based reasoning (TheoremQA), formal logic (LogicBench), tool-interleaved QA (ToolQA), medical calculation (MedCalc-Bench), competition mathematics (CHAMP), and code generation (BigCodeBench). Core problem is retrieving and applying reusable 'skills' (capability packages) for LLM agents.
problem_setting: Defines Skill Retrieval Augmentation (SRA): a single LLM agent must, on demand, retrieve relevant reusable skills from a large external skill corpus (26,262 skills, only 2.4% gold), decide whether/which to incorporate, and apply them to solve a task. Setting is largely offline/single-pass per query (a 'direct' engine statically prepends retrieved skills) but also includes interactive/iterative agentic engines (Progressive Disclosure with up to 10 load rounds; ReAct and ReAct+Progressive-Disclosure for ToolQA). Single-agent, no agent memory write-back; supervision = gold-skill annotations + ground-truth answers, used for decomposed evaluation (retrieval / incorporation / application), not to train models. Models are used zero-shot off-the-shelf (no fine-tuning of the LLM or retriever). The paper is primarily a paradigm formulation + benchmark + systematic empirical study (SR-Agents as a baseline family) rather than a single new method.
what_is_retrieved: skills: modular reusable capability packages. Each skill s=(name n, short description r, main content c [NL instructions, usage constraints, procedural guidance, SKILL.md-style markdown], executable payload pi [code/tools/auxiliary resources]). Distinct from declarative documents (RAG) and isolated tool APIs (function calling).
retrieval_grounding: STATIC external corpus: a fixed, large, noisy skill corpus (26,262 skills) collected from the web (GitHub, Skills.sh, Hugging Face Hub) plus 636 manually-constructed gold skills. The agent does NOT write back new skills; the corpus is frozen for evaluation. (The paper discusses lifelong/growing skill libraries and skill evolution only as future-agenda directions, not implemented.)
completeness_vs_topk_objective: Mixed. Retrieval is evaluated as fixed top-k ranking (Recall@K, nDCG@K; K in {1,10}). For multi-label datasets (CHAMP, BigCodeBench) an instance maps to MULTIPLE gold skills, so coverage of the complete needed set matters (instances grouped by whether at least one gold appears in top-50). The paper argues retrieval should ultimately be judged by downstream UTILITY (whether retrieved candidates close the agent's capability gap) rather than ranking alone, and floats utility-aware / set-retrieval objectives as future work. Practical configs mostly inject top-1 (Full-Skill Injection) or select 1 from top-50 (LLM Selection).
cbr_cycle_coverage: N/A (not framed as CBR). Mapping to CBR phases: Retrieve = yes (skill retrieval); Reuse = yes (skill incorporation + application); Revise = no (skills are not adapted to the instance beyond the agent reading them; the paper deliberately preserves an 'application gap'); Retain = no (no write-back of new/used skills). So effectively [Retrieve, Reuse] only.
explicit_cbr_grounding: False. The work does not frame itself as case-based reasoning and does not cite Aamodt & Plaza / Kolodner; it positions SRA as a capability-centric counterpart to RAG ('RAG retrieves knowledge; SRA retrieves capabilities') and a generalization beyond tool-use/function-calling.
retrieval_unit: skill (capability package): name + short description + procedural content + optional executable code/resources. Granularity is a reusable skill artifact (markdown SKILL.md-style), coarser than a single tool-API and richer than a passage. In Progressive Disclosure / LLM Selection, a compact index unit (name + description) is retrieved/exposed first, then the full skill content is loaded on demand.
index_source: Static corpus, offline-induced. 636 gold skills built via two-stage process (LLM draft then expert revision) from six source benchmarks, plus 25,626 web-collected distractor skills crawled from GitHub / Skills.sh / Hugging Face Hub, normalized to a unified document format. No online/test-time induction of the store.
index_structure_topology: Flat index over independently-indexed skills (sparse: BM25/TF-IDF term index; dense: BGE / Contriever vector index; plus a round-robin hybrid fusing BM25 and BGE ranked lists). No graph/hierarchy/cluster structure is used. (Structured organization—graphs, hierarchies, dependency structures over skills—is explicitly proposed only as future-agenda direction in §7.)
retriever_type: Compares sparse (BM25, TF-IDF), dense (BGE = BAAI/bge-base-en-v1.5; Contriever = facebook/contriever-msmarco), hybrid (round-robin interleaving of BM25 and BGE ranked lists), and LLM-as-reranker (the target LLM reranks BM25 top-50). BM25 is the default first-stage retriever in the main experiments.
retriever_learning_signal: None / off-the-shelf. All first-stage retrievers are used without task-specific training (BM25, TF-IDF, pretrained BGE and Contriever checkpoints). The LLM reranker is a frozen, zero-shot prompted LLM (no fine-tuning). The paper proposes utility-aware / end-task-feedback-trained retrieval only as a future direction; it is not implemented here.
query_construction: Raw user query / task prompt is used directly as the retrieval query against skill descriptions and content. For LLM Selection and Progressive Disclosure, the LLM is additionally given the candidate metadata (name + description) and selects/loads skills (an LLM-driven selection over the retrieved pool), but the first-stage retrieval query is the raw input. No query decomposition or synthetic expansion in the main method (intermediate-reasoning-state-conditioned retrieval is future work).
query_granularity: Primarily task-level (one-shot at t=0): retrieval is issued once per query for Full-Skill Injection / LLM Selection. For agentic engines (Progressive Disclosure with up to 10 load rounds; ReAct / ReAct+Progressive-Disclosure on ToolQA), skill incorporation/loading is decided step/turn-level, but the underlying skill RETRIEVAL is typically the single top-50 pool; loading from that pool is interleaved with reasoning.
when_to_retrieve: Retrieval (first-stage) is one-shot per query. Skill loading/incorporation is one-shot (direct injection) for Full-Skill Injection, and agent-initiated / iterative for Progressive Disclosure and ReAct-style engines (the model issues LOAD_SKILL actions on demand across turns).
retrieval_trigger_signal: First-stage retrieval: fixed schedule (always retrieve a candidate pool per query). Skill incorporation/loading trigger: agent-initiated request — in Progressive Disclosure the model decides whether and when to emit a 'LOAD_SKILL: <index>' action; in Full-Skill Injection injection is unconditional. A key empirical finding (RQ5/RQ6) is that this agent-initiated trigger is poorly calibrated: loading is neither reliably relevance-aware (independent of whether a gold skill is in the pool) nor need-aware (independent of whether the task exceeds native capability).
reranking: Yes — LLM-based reranking as an optional second stage: given BM25 top-50 candidates, the target LLM reranks them by relevance (listwise LLM reranker, following Sun et al. 2023). 'BM25 + Rerank' is consistently the strongest retrieval strategy in both intrinsic retrieval (Tables 3/4) and end-to-end (Table 5). No trained cross-encoder; hybrid uses round-robin list interleaving (not RRF-weighted) of BM25+BGE.
retrieved_context_refinement: Progressive disclosure / index-content separation: candidates are first exposed as compact metadata (name + description) and only the selected/loaded skill's full content is injected, limiting distractor exposure. LLM Selection narrows top-50 to a single skill before full injection. LLM reranking reorders candidates. No decompose-recompose, reason-in-documents distillation, or compression of skill content itself.
tool_document_engineering: Gold skills are engineered offline: standardized markdown artifacts with name, one-line description, and procedural content stating what the capability is, when it applies, how to use it, and common pitfalls; executable resources (e.g., Python implementations of medical calculators) attached when needed. Construction enforces generality, correctness, and leakage control (preserving an 'application gap'). Web distractor skills are normalized to a unified document format. Retrievers index over this raw/normalized skill text; no synthetic-query augmentation or instruction-tuned skill embeddings are used.
index_content_separation: Yes — a core design lever. LLM Selection and especially Progressive Disclosure separate a lightweight index (skill name + description catalog) from the heavy full skill content, which is loaded only on demand (OpenClaw-style progressive disclosure). This is shown to be more robust to distractors and to large top-k than Full-Skill Injection.
dynamic_index_and_protocol: Static skill corpus (frozen for evaluation); no live tool sync / CRUD. Integration protocol for skill use is in-context injection plus an explicit LOAD_SKILL action protocol (Progressive Disclosure) and a ReAct tool-call loop for ToolQA. Models are served via OpenAI-compatible endpoints. Not MCP/RapidAPI-based; live-synchronized tool indices are future work.
tool_dependency_awareness: No. Skills are treated as independently-indexed units with no modeling of inter-skill dependencies (prerequisites, alternatives, composition). The paper explicitly flags dependency/graph/hierarchy structure over skills as an open future-agenda direction (§7 'From unstructured skill collections to structured skill libraries').
how_retrieved_used: Prompt augmentation / skill reuse: the full content of selected retrieved skill(s) is prepended to the task prompt ('Relevant Skill: {skill content} {original user prompt}'), and the agent applies the skill's methodology. Three practical strategies: Full-Skill Injection (inject top-1 / top-k full content), LLM Selection (pick 1 from top-50 metadata then inject), Progressive Disclosure (compact catalog + on-demand LOAD_SKILL). Oracle Skill (inject gold) is the upper bound; LLM Direct (no skill) is the lower baseline. No training-signal or latent-token injection (parametric skill augmentation is proposed as future work).
planning_integration: Mostly retrieve-then-solve with one-shot exemplar-style injection at solve time (direct engine). For Progressive Disclosure and ReAct-based engines, skill loading is interleaved per-step/per-turn within the reasoning/acting loop (the model can load skills across up to 10 rounds; ReAct interleaves tool calls). Not embedded in MCTS/tree search; no explicit hierarchical subtask decomposition of retrieval.
reasoning_search_interleaving_granularit: Per-answer for Full-Skill Injection and LLM Selection (single retrieval+injection then generate). Per-turn / per-tool-call for the agentic engines: Progressive Disclosure interleaves skill-loading decisions across reasoning turns; ReAct (ToolQA) interleaves tool calls with reasoning.
retrieved_item_representation: Free-text procedural skill artifact (markdown: name, description, when/how-to-use, pitfalls) optionally bundled with executable program/code (e.g., Python calculator implementations). Injected verbatim as prompt text once loaded; in catalog form, represented as a compact name+description line.
abstraction_level_of_retrieved_unit: Procedural skill / reusable capability package: distilled, generalized 'how-to-solve-a-class-of-problems' procedures (theorem application method, logic-pattern, tool-use workflow, medical-calculator procedure, math concept, software-library usage) rather than raw trajectories or single demonstrations. Deliberately written above the instance level (leakage control preserves an application gap so the agent must still instantiate the procedure).
noise_robustness_mechanism: Controlled skill exposure / selective loading: Progressive Disclosure (expose only metadata, load full content on demand) and LLM Selection (narrow to one skill) reduce distractor interference and are shown markedly more robust than Full-Skill Injection under hard-negative distractors and large top-k. LLM reranking improves top-rank precision. However, the paper's central negative finding is that current LLMs lack reliable relevance-aware and need-aware loading, so robustness remains limited; no retriever-aware training or distractor-aware SFT is applied (these are proposed as future work).
memory_type: none (with respect to a growing agent memory). The skill corpus is a static external skill-library used for retrieval, not an episodic/working memory the agent updates. No procedural/graph/latent memory is maintained across tasks.
write_back: False. The system does not store new experiences/cases/skills during evaluation; the skill corpus is fixed. Lifelong skill accumulation, offline skill refinement, and skill evolution are discussed only as future-agenda directions (§7).
online_growth: False. The retrievable store is frozen after offline construction; it does not grow at test time.
failure_experience_usage: Not used. Failed trajectories/experiences are not stored or retrieved (no memory). The paper does analyze failure modes diagnostically (skill-loading hallucination; lack of need-awareness) and proposes feedback-driven skill debugging/refinement as future work, but does not implement failure-experience storage or contrastive success/failure retrieval.
memory_evolution_update: N/A — the skill store is static (append-free after offline construction); no dedup-merge/delta-update/refine-overwrite/prune is performed at runtime. (Offline skill optimization/evolution is future-agenda only.)
retrieval_as_learned_policy: No. Retrieval/selection is a fixed similarity top-k (BM25/TF-IDF/BGE/Contriever/hybrid) plus an optional zero-shot LLM reranker and LLM-based selection; none is trained/RL-optimized. The skill-loading decision is made by a frozen LLM via prompting (not a learned policy). Training retrievers from end-task utility feedback and learned controlled-exposure policies are proposed as future research.
cross_agent_or_cross_framework_sharing: Single-agent; no cross-agent shared memory. However, the skill corpus is a SHARED external resource and skills are framed as plug-and-play reusable capabilities portable across agents/models. The benchmark is evaluated across multiple heterogeneous LLM families (Qwen3, Llama, Mistral, GLM-5.1, GPT-5.4) using the same corpus, but this is cross-model evaluation, not collaborative shared memory among concurrently running agents.
benchmarks: SRA-Bench (newly introduced) = six capability-intensive source datasets re-purposed with gold-skill annotations: TheoremQA (747 inst / 320 skills), LogicBench (760 / 19), ToolQA (1,430 / 14), MedCalc-Bench (1,100 / 55), CHAMP (223 / 89, multi-label), BigCodeBench (1,140 / 139, multi-label). Total 5,400 instances, 636 unique gold skills, mixed with 25,626 web distractor skills into a 26,262-skill retrieval corpus (2.4% gold).
benchmark_family: Composite capability benchmark spanning QA/reasoning (TheoremQA, CHAMP competition math, LogicBench formal logic), tool-use (ToolQA), domain calculation (MedCalc-Bench), and code (BigCodeBench). Plus a skill-retrieval IR benchmark over a 26k-skill corpus (Recall@K / nDCG@K). Not aligned to a single prior family (Mind2Web/WebArena/ALFWorld/ToolBench/etc.).
baselines: Skill-use strategies: LLM Direct (no skill, lower bound), Oracle Skill (gold injected, upper bound), Full-Skill Injection (BM25 top-1 full content), LLM Selection (pick 1 from BM25 top-50 metadata), Progressive Disclosure (OpenClaw-style on-demand loading from top-50). Retrievers compared: BM25, TF-IDF, BGE, Contriever, Hybrid (BM25+BGE round-robin), BM25+LLM Rerank. Models: Qwen3-4B/32B/235B-A22B, Llama-3.1-8B-Instruct, Llama-3.3-70B-Instruct, Mistral-Small-3.1-24B-Instruct-2503; behavioral analyses (RQ5/RQ6) also include GLM-5.1 and GPT-5.4.
key_metrics: Retrieval: Recall@K and nDCG@K (K in {1,10}). End-task: rule-based exact-match/accuracy for TheoremQA/LogicBench/ToolQA/CHAMP/MedCalc-Bench; pass@1 via unit-test execution for BigCodeBench. Behavioral: skill-loading rate (% of instances where the agent incorporates >=1 valid skill before answering), and load-rate differences between gold-covered vs not (RQ5) and skill-free-correct vs skill-free-wrong (RQ6).
headline_result: Retrieval-based skill augmentation substantially improves agents but lags the oracle. Example (Llama-3.3-70B average over 6 datasets): LLM Direct 47.8 -> LLM Selection 59.2 -> Oracle Skill 64.4. The strongest practical config is LLM Selection (most stable retrieval-to-task transfer) and BM25+Rerank (best retriever); e.g. for Qwen3-235B, BM25+Rerank averages 62.6 vs BM25 56.2 and LLM Direct 53.3. Central negative finding: skill-loading rates are nearly identical regardless of whether a gold skill was retrieved (RQ5) or whether the task exceeds native capability (RQ6; Overall Delta Load = +0.1pp), revealing missing relevance- and need-awareness.
ablations: RQ2 robustness: (a) controlled hard-negative distractors N in {0,2,4,8} with gold always present — Full-Skill Injection degrades sharply, Progressive Disclosure stays stable; brittleness does not vanish with model scale. (b) BM25 top-k sweep k in {1,2,4,8} — Full-Skill Injection improves only at small k then declines (inter-skill interference), Progressive Disclosure stable. RQ3: retriever comparison (Recall@1/10, nDCG@1/10) — no universal winner among sparse/dense; BGE generally > Contriever; hybrid mainly raises top-10 recall; LLM rerank strongest, not monotonic in scale. RQ4: end-to-end under 5 retrievers — BM25+Rerank most consistent gains but retrieval gains not strictly monotonic into task gains. RQ5/RQ6: relevance- and need-awareness of skill loading (gold-in-top-50 vs not; skill-free-correct vs wrong) — weak/absent for most models, sharper relevance-awareness only at 235B scale and in GLM-5.1/GPT-5.4.
evaluation_decoupling: Yes — a central contribution. SRA-Bench decomposes evaluation into skill retrieval (intrinsic Recall@K/nDCG@K, Tables 3/4), skill incorporation (skill-loading rate and relevance/need-awareness, Tables 6/7/8), and end-task execution (accuracy/pass@1, Tables 2/5), reported separately, enabling diagnosis of where the pipeline fails.
process_vs_outcome_metrics: Both. Outcome: end-task accuracy / pass@1. Process: intrinsic retrieval quality (Recall/nDCG), and especially incorporation-process metrics — skill-loading rate, relevance-awareness (load-rate gap for gold-in-top-50 vs not), and need-awareness (load-rate gap for skill-free-wrong vs correct). These process metrics drive the paper's main diagnostic findings.
cost_efficiency_tradeoff: Motivation is context-budget efficiency: enumerating all skills in-context fails to scale (context limits + selection-accuracy degradation), so retrieval narrows N=26,262 to k<<N. Progressive Disclosure / index-content separation reduce token exposure by loading full content only on demand (up to 10 load rounds). No explicit latency/API-cost/token-count numbers are reported; models served with 128K context, temperature 0.7. Parametric Skill Augmentation (turning head skills into plug-in parameters to amortize repeated injection cost) is proposed as future efficiency work.
context_budget_and_selection_count: Practical configs: Full-Skill Injection injects BM25 top-1 (or top-k in the sweep, k in {1,2,4,8}) full skill content; LLM Selection and Progressive Disclosure operate over a BM25 top-50 candidate pool but inject only the selected/loaded skill's full content (catalog = name+description). Distractor study uses gold + N in {0,2,4,8} hard negatives. Models served with 128K-token context. k is largely fixed per config; selection is precision-driven (pick 1) for LLM Selection.
survey_scope_and_axes: N/A (not a survey). It is a paradigm-formulation + benchmark + systematic empirical study organized around six research questions (RQ1 usefulness, RQ2 noise robustness, RQ3 retriever effectiveness, RQ4 retrieval->task transfer, RQ5 relevance-aware loading, RQ6 need-aware loading).
benchmark_construction_and_size: Size: 5,400 test instances, 636 manually-constructed gold skills, 26,262-skill retrieval corpus (636 gold + 25,626 web distractors; 2.4% gold). Construction: reverse-engineered — start from capability-intensive instances in six existing benchmarks, abstract source signals (theorem/logic-pattern/calculator/concept/library names) into standardized markdown gold skills via LLM draft + expert revision (principles: generality, correctness, leakage control with preserved application gap); distractors crawled from GitHub/Skills.sh/HF and normalized. Answer verifiability: rule-based exact-match for five datasets, unit-test execution (pass@1) for BigCodeBench. Difficulty signal: even strongest models stay well below Oracle Skill (e.g., best practical averages ~62-63 vs oracles ~64-68), and skill retrieval Recall@1 is low on several datasets (e.g., LogicBench/ToolQA/CHAMP), showing the benchmark is far from saturated.
builds_on: Retrieval-Augmented Generation (Lewis et al. 2020) and its retrieve-then-read pipeline; classic retrievers BM25 (Robertson et al.), TF-IDF (Sparck Jones), Contriever (Izacard et al.), BGE/C-Pack (Xiao et al.); hybrid fusion (Bruch et al. 2023); LLM-as-reranker (Sun et al. 2023); agent-skill systems, esp. Voyager (Wang et al. 2023, growing skill library of executable programs) and OpenClaw-style SKILL.md progressive disclosure; tool-use/function-calling (Toolformer, Gorilla, ToolLLM, BFCL). Source datasets: TheoremQA, LogicBench, ToolQA, MedCalc-Bench, CHAMP, BigCodeBench.
contrasts_with: Classical knowledge-centric RAG (retrieves declarative evidence) — SRA retrieves executable capabilities judged by downstream utility, not just semantic relevance. Conventional tool-use/function-calling (assumes a small visible API set; e.g., Toolformer, Gorilla, ToolLLM/BFCL) — SRA retrieves from an open-ended out-of-context corpus of richer skill packages. In-context skill enumeration (OpenClaw/Codex/Claude Code SKILL.md injection) — shown not to scale. SkillsBench (Li et al. 2026) — evaluates whether curated skills help, but does not decompose retrieval/incorporation/application; SRA-Bench does.
lineage: Group C (RAG + planning / agentic): a 2026 reframing of retrieval-augmentation as capability augmentation for agents — sits at the intersection of RAG, tool retrieval, and agent skills. Extends the static-corpus RAG/tool-retrieval line (BM25/dense/hybrid/rerank) to executable skill packages, introduces a decomposed retrieval/incorporation/application evaluation, and points toward utility-aware skill retrieval, structured skill libraries, and parametric skill augmentation as the forward lineage.
adaptation_mechanism: N/A (not CBR). Retrieved skills are used as verbatim in-context procedural guidance (prepended) and applied by the LLM; there is no explicit case-adaptation/revision step (the benchmark deliberately preserves an application gap so the agent must still instantiate the procedure to the instance).
